units.function: find the one stat that decides it
units.reusable_pattern: give the difference, concede the rest are close, then name the cause of the loss
prohibited_generalizations: Credit the whole stat line for the result.

units.source_excerpt: Sabalenka consistently maintained a lead by scoring consecutive points. With her strong momentum, she easily secured victory in the first set. Starting with the second set, she began to commit unforced errors, resulting in a shift of momentum.
units.function: narrate the shift
units.reusable_pattern: give the lead, the cause of the win, then the errors that move the momentum
reusable_elements: resulting in a shift of momentum
prohibited_generalizations: Report the score without the momentum.

units.source_excerpt: At this juncture, the disparity in momentum was not significant; hence, Guaff emerged victorious by a narrow margin. Sabalenka's significant decline was primarily due to her high number of unforced errors. Consequently, she suffered a substantial defeat.
units.function: tie the margin to the gap
units.reusable_pattern: connect a small gap to a narrow win, then a large drop to a heavy loss
information_order: small gap, narrow win, large drop, heavy loss
prohibited_generalizations: Correct the printed spelling of the name.

units.source_excerpt: Through the above analysis, combined with the technical statistics, the actual situation of the game, and the visualization of the game flow, we can find that the model can be adapted to different types of games, with an excellent generalization ability.
units.function: pile three supports under one claim
units.reusable_pattern: name the three sources, then the claim they jointly support
reusable_elements: Through the above analysis, combined with
can be adapted to different types of games
prohibited_generalizations: Claim generalization from one match alone.

units.source_excerpt: The model works better. However, there are still some deficiencies that need to be considered in future models, which are summarized.
units.function: pivot from success to deficiencies
units.reusable_pattern: grant the result, then announce the deficiencies as a list
reusable_elements: However, there are still some deficiencies
prohibited_generalizations: List deficiencies with no link to the result.

units.source_excerpt: Referees and players may not be consistent in their judgment, and it is reasonable to expect wrong judgments and disputes. When the penalties exceed the preparation and past experience, it will sharply reduce the momentum, leading to a critical response and causing heart fluctuations.
units.function: trace a bad call to the momentum
units.reusable_pattern: grant that errors are reasonable, then trace the excessive one to the collapse
prohibited_generalizations: Blame every call for the collapse.

units.source_excerpt: Under high competition stress, athletes' psychological reactions differ from normal. Some athletes can quickly detach from the low momentum, while others will be immersed in it for a long time.
units.function: split athletes by recovery
units.reusable_pattern: state the condition, then divide athletes into those who detach and those who stay
prohibited_generalizations: Treat all athletes as equally resilient.

units.source_excerpt: If your athlete has lost to the other athlete, or if the other is a veteran whose strength is well known, your athlete will overestimate the opponent's strength and develop fear and stage fright, which will seriously reduce your momentum.
units.function: address the coach directly
units.reusable_pattern: give two conditions, then the fear, then the effect on momentum
prohibited_generalizations: Keep the warning in the third person.

units.source_excerpt: On hard courts the Russians, Americans, and French win the most. On clay the same three. On turf the Americans, Russians, and Australians. On carpet the Russians, the French, and the Australians. This has to do with their country's training grounds. When an athlete plays on a field they are familiar with, their momentum will increase.
units.function: list the venues then give one cause
units.reusable_pattern: give four venues with their top nations, then one cause that covers all four
reusable_elements: it will be easier to get into shape
prohibited_generalizations: Give a different cause for each surface.

units.source_excerpt: When a player scores and the audience cheers, the applause also increases his momentum. If a player loses and the audience boos or even applauds out of dissatisfaction, the player's momentum will be seriously affected, and his game status will be in tatters.
units.function: give the crowd both directions
units.reusable_pattern: show the cheer raising momentum and the boo destroying it
prohibited_generalizations: Count only the scoring and ignore the crowd.

units.source_excerpt: In order to quantitatively model momentum, we have already determined two significant factors, the sliding window size and the out-of-play advantage of a player's serve. These parameters are now being modified to simulate various types of matches with varied serve advantages.
units.function: restate the two parameters before testing them
units.reusable_pattern: name both parameters again, then say they are being varied
reusable_elements: are now being modified to simulate
prohibited_generalizations: Vary a parameter the reader has not been reminded of.

units.source_excerpt: To enhance the presentation of the findings, we calculate the disparity in momentum between the two players. Assuming player 1 as the reference, when the curve lies below the axis the momentum is on the other side, and vice versa.
units.function: define the plotted quantity
units.reusable_pattern: say why the difference is plotted, then how to read the sign
prohibited_generalizations: Plot a difference without saying which side is positive.

units.source_excerpt: When subjected to a specific perturbation of the two parameters, the disparity undergoes a discernible alteration, particularly when the window size is modified. However, overall, the trajectory stays unaltered. Put simply, the model effectively captures the player's condition over various matches.
units.function: separate the change from the shape
units.reusable_pattern: grant the alteration, localize it, then say the trajectory holds, then restate plainly
prohibited_generalizations: Call the model robust without saying what did change.

units.source_excerpt: Hence, it is logical and justifiable that the curve may undergo significant changes at certain nodes. The pattern of the sensitivity test curve aligns with the actual condition once again, overall.
units.function: defend the changes and close
units.reusable_pattern: call the large changes logical, then say the pattern matches reality again
reusable_elements: it is logical and justifiable that
aligns with the actual condition once again, overall
prohibited_generalizations: Treat every change as a failure.

units.source_excerpt: The model is systematic. When selecting metrics, this model encompasses the entirety of the race, rather than examining only a single segment. Makes the results more relevant.
units.function: claim coverage of the whole match
units.reusable_pattern: name the virtue, say what is covered, then the consequence
prohibited_generalizations: Repair the sentence that has no subject.

units.source_excerpt: When calculating the momentum, the scores of both the enemy and the opponent are considered at the same time, and the calculation results are more in line with reality.
units.function: claim both sides are counted
units.reusable_pattern: name the two sides and the realism that follows
reusable_elements: more in line with the reality
prohibited_generalizations: Keep the printed pairing of enemy and opponent as if it were a distinction.

units.source_excerpt: When studying whether momentum affects the game, two models, the tour test and the chi-square test, were used for comparative analysis, so as to make the results more accurate.
units.function: justify two tests by comparison
units.reusable_pattern: name both tests and the accuracy the comparison buys
reusable_elements: so as to make the results more accurate
prohibited_generalizations: Correct the printed name of the test.

units.source_excerpt: This model is only applicable to individual matches. Team momentum is not simply the sum of individual momentum. If we want to solve the momentum of group matches, we also need to consider the impact of teammates' scores or losses on each other's momentum.
units.function: bound the model and name the missing term
units.reusable_pattern: state the limit, deny the obvious extension, then name what a team model would need
prohibited_generalizations: Claim the model extends to teams.

units.source_excerpt: Optimisation algorithms such as Bayesian tuning can be combined to further optimise the hyperparameters. The main method is to fit a proxy model with known hyperparameters and results, then use the acquisition function to select the next best pair, and repeat.
units.function: describe the improvement not made
units.reusable_pattern: name the method, then give its loop, and leave it as future work
reusable_elements: can be combined to further optimise
prohibited_generalizations: Present the tuning as work already done.

units.source_excerpt: Initially, we constructed a momentum quantification model using a sliding-window approach. This involved specifying the size of the window and evaluating the momentum by considering the performance in each metric during that window.
units.function: restate the first model
units.reusable_pattern: open the conclusion on the first model and its two ingredients
prohibited_generalizations: Open the conclusion on the result.

units.source_excerpt: In the model, we incorporate the extra benefit of the player's serve to replicate the fact that the serving player has a greater likelihood of winning.
units.function: restate the serve term as realism
units.reusable_pattern: give the term and the fact it is there to copy
prohibited_generalizations: Mention the serve term without its purpose.

units.source_excerpt: Subsequently, by employing the run test and the chi-square test, it was determined that momentum plays a pivotal role. Hence, it is imperative for coaches and players to acknowledge the significance of momentum.
units.function: turn the tests into a duty
units.reusable_pattern: name both tests, give the finding, then the obligation
prohibited_generalizations: Leave the finding inside the tests.

units.source_excerpt: Afterwards, the data distribution is examined through principal component analysis in order to construct the prediction model. This model exhibits a higher level of accuracy, reaching up to 70 percent. Additionally, it identifies significant factors such as the double fault, the ace, and consecutive scores.
units.function: restate the accuracy and the factors
units.reusable_pattern: give the purpose, the accuracy with its ceiling, then the factors
prohibited_generalizations: Quote the accuracy without the words reaching up to.

units.source_excerpt: On this basis, we evaluate the model, assess its capacity to generalize, and conduct sensitivity tests. The analysis indicates that the model exhibits exceptional performance, possesses a high degree of generalization, demonstrates resilience, and can be easily modified for different types of matches.
units.function: stack four virtues
units.reusable_pattern: list the three checks, then the four virtues they support
reusable_elements: exhibits, possesses, demonstrates, and can be
prohibited_generalizations: Claim one virtue and stop.

units.source_excerpt: Ultimately, we furnish tennis coaches with insights into the significance of momentum and offer guidance on how players can sustain and control momentum throughout a match.
units.function: close on the coaches
units.reusable_pattern: end on the two things given to the coaches
prohibited_generalizations: Close on the model's accuracy.

units.source_excerpt: Four references: a journal article on momentum at the US Open, a master's thesis on key points, a doctoral thesis on the fluctuate phenomenon, and a runs test paper in an epidemiology journal.
units.function: list the four sources
units.reusable_pattern: give each source its form, and keep the one from outside the sport
prohibited_generalizations: Drop the source that sits outside the topic.

units.source_excerpt: To the coaches and players, from the team, dated the fifth of February 2024, on momentum comprehension, mastery, and application.
units.function: give the memo its header
units.reusable_pattern: give the recipient, the sender, the date, and a subject in three parts
prohibited_generalizations: Start the memo without its header.

units.source_excerpt: Dear sir or madam: Everyone desires success on the court, and our research indicates that momentum could be of assistance to you.
units.function: open on the reader's desire
units.reusable_pattern: name what the reader wants, then offer the research as help
reusable_elements: could be of assistance to you
prohibited_generalizations: Open the memo on the model.

units.source_excerpt: We have determined, through an analysis of past tennis matches, that momentum is a critical factor. Players have the ability to reverse the ultimate result of a match by utilizing the force of momentum.
units.function: state the finding and its power
units.reusable_pattern: give the finding with its evidence, then the reversal it makes possible
reusable_elements: We have determined, through an analysis
prohibited_generalizations: Promise a reversal with no analysis behind it.

units.source_excerpt: A participant with momentum will experience a sense that everything is proceeding in their favor. The player will be playing with increased assurance, and the momentum will assist in sustaining that assurance.
units.function: describe the feeling
units.reusable_pattern: give the feeling first, then the assurance, then the loop
reusable_elements: a sense that everything is proceeding in their favor
prohibited_generalizations: Define momentum again instead of describing it.

units.source_excerpt: A shift in momentum does not warrant a loss of confidence. Maintaining perseverance and a positive mindset are critical factors in regaining the upper hand. However, the player might be required to alter their playing manner or return to their initial approach.
units.function: separate the shift from the response
units.reusable_pattern: deny the loss of confidence, name what regains the lead, then concede a change of style
prohibited_generalizations: Tell the player never to change.

units.source_excerpt: Based on our analysis of the results, we propose the following recommendations.
units.function: tie the advice to the results
units.reusable_pattern: ground the list in the analysis before giving it
reusable_elements: Based on our analysis of the results, we propose
prohibited_generalizations: Start the list with no basis.

units.source_excerpt: Coaches ought to prioritize the cultivation of psychological qualities, so that referee errors and missed opportunities do not damage the players' confidence.
units.function: give the coach one duty
units.reusable_pattern: name the duty and the harm it prevents
reusable_elements: ought to prioritize the cultivation of
prohibited_generalizations: Give the duty with no purpose.

units.source_excerpt: Players ought to allocate physical energy judiciously; if physical energy is consumed too rapidly, the momentum value will remain in a comparatively low state.
units.function: tie the pacing to the value
units.reusable_pattern: give the instruction, then the consequence of ignoring it
reusable_elements: will remain in a comparatively low state
prohibited_generalizations: Advise pacing with no link to the model.

units.source_excerpt: Of course, our model only plays the role of prediction, but it can be enough to help you. Thank you for reading our memo again in your busy schedule, and we hope our suggestions are useful to you.
units.function: concede the limit and thank the reader
units.reusable_pattern: concede the model only predicts, claim that is enough, then thank the reader
prohibited_generalizations: Close by restating the accuracy.
